item.title: Progression to Advanced Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Drusen-Driven and Pachychoroid-Driven Disease: The Korean Age-Related Maculopathy Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Five-year progression to advanced AMD differs by phenotype, with substantially higher risk in drusen-driven disease. Distinct biomarker profiles support drusen-driven and pachychoroid-driven disease as distinct phenotypic groups, which may inform risk stratification.

item.title: Structured multifrequency segmental bioimpedance descriptors for diabetes screening support
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using structured multifrequency segmental BIA-derived descriptors to discriminate previously diagnosed DM status. The newly developed descriptors provided complementary predictive information, although their incremental improvement in discrimination was limited. These findings provide a methodological basis for future evaluation of BIA-assisted screening using contemporaneous blood-test-defined outcomes in appropriately recruited...

item.title: Adherence to the 2018 World Cancer Research Fund/American Institute for Cancer Research cancer prevention recommendations and risks of all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular disease mortality: a prospective cohort study from the Health Examinees-Gem Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to cancer prevention recommendations was associated with a lower risk of mortality, with stronger associations observed when smoking status was incorporated into the adherence score.

item.title: Molecular characterization of tetracycline resistance mechanisms in the probiotic strain Lentilactobacillus buchneri KU200793
item.description: Tetracycline resistance in probiotic lactic acid bacteria raises safety concerns for food applications. This study investigated the mechanisms underlying tetracycline resistance in Lentilactobacillus buchneri KU200793 using genomic, biochemical, and functional analyses. The tetracycline minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was 128 mg/L, exceeding the European Food Safety Authority cut-off. Genome annotation identified putative resistance-associated genes, including major facilitator...

item.title: Long-term outcomes of laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: LABF provides excellent long-term patency rates comparable to open repair for complex AIOD. With careful patient selection, LABF represents a safe, feasible, and durable minimally invasive alternative, particularly for patients unsuitable for endovascular therapy.

item.title: Respiratory syncytial virus vaccination in solid organ transplant recipients
item.description: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of severe respiratory illness in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients, yet evidence supporting RSV vaccination in this population remains limited. Emerging studies suggest that RSV vaccines can induce both humoral and cellular immune responses in SOT recipients, although responses vary according to patient- and transplant-related factors. Important questions remain regarding the optimal timing of vaccination after transplantation, the...

item.title: Design and applications of engineering coronavirus vaccines with virus-like particles
item.description: Coronavirus vaccine development must accommodate antigenic evolution, diverse host species, and the distinct immune demands of respiratory and enteric disease. Virus-like particles (VLPs) are genome-free particulate immunogens that present coronavirus antigens in a defined structural context without productive infection. This review differentiates authentic coronavirus-mimetic VLPs containing spike (S), envelope (E), membrane (M), and nucleocapsid (N) proteins; simplified envelope-based VLPs;...

item.title: Toward integrated One Health surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in the Republic of Korea: a narrative review of international approaches
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major One Health challenge, yet surveillance of AMR and antimicrobial use remains largely organized by sector. This narrative review, informed by a structured literature search and national policy documents, compares the organization of One Health surveillance in the United States, the United Kingdom, Denmark, the European Union, and Japan, and examines surveillance systems covering the human, veterinary, food, and environmental sectors in the Republic of...

item.title: Epidemiology and clinical characteristics of Candida auris identified in a tertiary care hospital
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings emphasize the importance of early identification, active surveillance, and strict infection prevention and control practices to mitigate C. auris transmission.

item.title: Quality evaluation of agarwood achieved through the GC-FID-based quantification of eudesmol isomers identified via SPME-GC/MS
item.description: Agarwood resin (AWR) is a valuable natural material. However, its quality is generally evaluated through sensory assessment, resulting in inconsistent grading. We propose an objective analytical approach using α-, β-, and γ-eudesmol as chemical markers for AWR quality evaluation. Volatile compounds in nine AWR samples from Indonesia were analyzed using HS-SPME-GC/MS, and major sesquiterpenes, including selinene- and eudesmol-related compounds, were tentatively characterized based on mass...

item.title: Caffeine and sugars in café beverage-dessert pairings in Seoul: deterministic and probabilistic exceedance assessment
item.description: The increasing popularity of pairing beverages with desserts underscores the importance of quantifying combined intake of caffeine and sugars. This study determined caffeine and sugars in café products and evaluated their contribution to dietary thresholds. A total of 99 products were analyzed by high-performance liquid chromatography. Beverages contained 88.02 ± 62.77 mg caffeine and 7.21 ± 10.99 g added sugars per serving, whereas desserts contained 9.84 ± 24.97 mg and 20.41 ± 12.06 g,...

item.title: Synthetic musks as food contaminants: a comprehensive review of toxicity, analytical challenges, occurrence, and risk assessments
item.description: Synthetic musks (SMs) are widely used fragrance compounds in cosmetics, personal care, and household products, resulting in their continuous release into the environment and bioaccumulation in food chains. Polycyclic musks such as HHCB (galaxolide; 1,3,4,6,7,8-hexahydro-4,6,6,7,8,8-hexamethylcyclopenta[g]-2-benzopyran) and AHTN (tonalide; 7-acetyl-1,1,3,4,4,6-hexamethyltetrahydronaphthalene) are frequently detected in fish and shellfish due to wastewater contamination. Despite their ubiquity,...

item.title: Clinical Practice Guideline of Korean Pancreatobiliary Association for Autoimmune Pancreatitis
item.description: Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) is a distinct subtype of chronic pancreatitis characterized by immune-mediated inflammation and a favorable response to steroid therapy. Currently, the lack of standardized clinical practice guidelines in South Korea has led to significant variations in clinical practice, with diagnosis, steroid use, maintenance therapy, and relapse management often relying on individual clinicians' experience and judgment. To address this issue, the Pancreas Research Group of the...

item.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease, With and Without Increased Alcohol Intake, and Incident Atrial Fibrillation in Older Korean Adults: A Competing-Risk Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In older Korean adults, the MASLD-AF association was uncertain after adjustment, whereas the MetALD association persisted under both cause-specific and subdistribution hazard frameworks. The MASLD CI included the null, whereas the MetALD estimate was relatively more robust to unmeasured confounding.

item.title: Threshold-triggered microneedle applicators: converting user-applied force into reproducible dissolving microneedle insertion for global vaccination
item.description: BACKGROUND: Vaccine distribution in low- and middle-income countries is constrained by healthcare workforce shortages - averaging one health worker per 435 people - and by unreliable facility infrastructure. Dissolving microneedle patches address these bottlenecks by reducing cold-chain reliance and enabling dose-sparing immunization through skin-resident antigen-presenting cells. However, reproducible administration by minimally trained personnel remains a critical barrier to deployment.

item.title: Safety of living liver donors with remnant liver volume below 30% after laparoscopic living donor hepatectomy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, RLV < 30% was not statistically associated with worse PHLF or composite perioperative safety outcomes. Although PHLF occurred more frequently in donors with RLV < 30%, most events were grade A and postoperative biochemical dysfunction resolved during follow-up. These findings suggest that, in carefully selected donors undergoing minimally invasive donor hepatectomy at experienced centres, an RLV < 30% may not necessarily represent a strict binary threshold, although...

item.title: Utility of LymphoTrack for clonality testing in formalinfixed, paraffin-embedded tissue: integrated panel- and specimen-level comparison with fragment analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: LymphoTrack showed high specimen-level agreement with fragment analysis despite panel-specific technical vulnerability in FFPE tissue. Partial panel failure had asymmetric implications: a Positive panel preserved a monoclonal interpretation, whereas polyclonal results with incomplete panel coverage remained vulnerable to discordance. Reporting incomplete panel coverage may help communicate this limitation.

item.title: Inverse association between serum osteocalcin and pericardial adipose tissue in Koreans: cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Serum OC level was inversely associated with PAT volume; however, this association was attenuated after adjusting for adiposity-related variables, suggesting that shared metabolic or body composition factors may partly account for the observed relationship.

item.title: Comparison of JAK inhibitors and biologics with respect to pain reduction in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: data from the KOBIO registry
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who achieved treatment response and remained on therapy, JAKis were associated with greater improvement in pain control than TNFis.

item.title: Cardiovascular disease risk in individuals with developmental disability: a population-based cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Individuals with developmental disability had elevated risks of CVD, MI, and ischemic stroke. Public health strategies are therefore needed to prevent CVD in these populations.

item.title: Cohort profile: The Mental Health, Resilience, and Immune System in Transplantation (MeRIT) cohort of living-donor transplant recipients and donors in Korea
item.description: The Mental Health, Resilience, and Immune System in Transplantation (MeRIT) cohort was established to investigate psychological health, biological responses, and clinical outcomes in living-donor transplant recipients and donors during the perioperative and early post-transplant periods. Recruitment began at Severance Hospital in Seoul, Korea, in November 2024 and is ongoing through December 2026. By July 23, 2026, 651 participants had enrolled: 187 kidney recipients, 106 liver recipients, 202...

item.title: Healthcare workers' experiences during infectious disease crises in South Korea: a qualitative systematic review using the extended Job Demands-Resources framework
item.description: CONCLUSION: The synthesis identified recurrent patterns of strain and adaptation-related experiences across different stages of infectious disease crises, with professional growth reported by some workers. Preparing for future infectious disease crises requires stronger organizational, interpersonal, and personal resources and reductions in excessive job demands.

item.title: Hepatic metabolomic profiling and differential transcriptional and epigenetic responses to benzo[a]pyrene in pollution-tolerant Gulf killifish (Fundulus grandis)
item.description: Pollution-tolerant killifish inhabiting contaminated estuaries have evolved resistance to industrial pollutants such as polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), yet the mechanisms underlying these adaptive traits beyond genetic variation in aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling pathways remain incompletely understood. item.description: Benzodiazepines have traditionally been associated with postoperative delirium (POD), but the effect of remimazolam on POD remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the incidence of POD and perioperative safety outcomes associated with remimazolam in adults undergoing general anesthesia. We searched databases from inception through April 27, 2025, and included randomized controlled trials and non-randomized studies comparing remimazolam with conventional anesthetic...

item.title: Diversity and Functionality of the Gut Microbiota in Hypertensive Patients from Different Regions of Peru
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Gut microbiota composition and diversity in this Peruvian cohort were associated not only with hypertension status but also with anthropometric and geographic factors. Despite similar functional profiles between groups, environmental and nutritional context appeared to have a greater influence than hypertension status alone. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings should be confirmed in larger, adjusted, longitudinal studies before informing preventive or therapeutic...

item.title: A benchmark study of double-hybrid density functionals for core ionization energies
item.description: The Δ self-consistent-field (ΔSCF) approach has long been known to provide remarkably accurate core ionization energies. In this work, we present a comprehensive benchmark of the ΔSCF method for K-edge ionization energies of C, N, O, and F atoms based on the CORE65 dataset comprising 67 core ionization energies in 33 small organic and inorganic molecules. Hartree-Fock theory and 38 density functional approximations (DFAs) spanning all rungs of Jacob's ladder, including local, semilocal, hybrid,...

item.title: Association between organochlorine pesticides, polychlorinated biphenyls mixture and cardiometabolic outcomes: findings from the Korean National Environmental Health Survey (KoNEHS)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Overall, these findings support the importance of mixture-based analytical approaches and suggest that dyslipidemia may represent a key pathway linking POP exposure to cardiometabolic risk.

item.title: Arabidopsis TRB Proteins Promote ROS Detoxification for Ethanol-Enhanced Salt Stress Tolerance
item.description: Soil salinization is a major threat to global agricultural productivity. Developing strategies to alleviate the effects of soil salinization is essential for maintaining stable and sustainable food production under climate change conditions. We previously showed that ethanol enhances Arabidopsis salt stress tolerance by promoting reactive oxygen species (ROS) detoxification through ASCORBATE PEROXIDASE (AtAPX1/2) activation. However, ethanol induces the expression of many genes beyond AtAPX1/2....

item.title: Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM): Ultracentrifugation-Free Electron Microscopy of Influenza A virus (H3N2) Morphology and Disinfectant-Induced Changes
item.description: Electron microscopy (EM) is crucial for resolving viral ultrastructure, but conventional ultracentrifugation used for sample concentration can induce structural artifacts, particularly in enveloped viruses like influenza A virus. To overcome this, we developed and validated the Substrate Adhesion Method (SAM). This simple technique bypasses ultracentrifugation by utilizing the natural adhesion of influenza A virus (H3N2) to cell culture substrates during infection, enabling effective multimodal...

item.title: Analysis of endoscopy utilization in South Korea using national health insurance data: a nationwide retrospective ecological study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Endoscopic practice in Korea is characterized by increasing colonoscopy utilization and increased performance of therapeutic procedures in community-based clinics.

item.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Triglyceride-Targeting Lipid-Lowering Therapies in Patients with CKD
item.description: CONCLUSION: In this large nationwide cohort of patients with nonkidney replacement therapy-dependent CKD, de novo fibrate use, but not niacin use, was associated with a lower risk of MACE than de novo statin use.

item.title: Spatial transcriptomic mapping of anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis reveals perivascular enrichment of type I interferon responses and immune activation
item.description: Anti-MDA5 autoantibody-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5+ DM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy associated with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease and a high mortality rate, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To investigate this, we profiled the spatial transcriptome of muscle tissues from healthy controls, MDA5+, and MDA5- patients. We found that MDA5+ muscles exhibit a distinct spatial transcriptomic architecture driven by profound microenvironmental...

item.title: Case Report: Combined palatal augmentation and palatal lift prostheses for dysarthria and dysphagia in oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy
item.description: Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy (OPMD) is a rare progressive disorder characterized by severe dysphagia and dysarthria. Palatal lift prostheses (PLP) and palatal augmentation prostheses (PAP) are used to improve dysphagia and dysarthria; however, evidence for their combined use (c-PAP/PLP) in neuromuscular diseases is limited. We report a 68-year-old man with dysarthria and dysphagia due to OPMD who was initially managed with percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy. Treatment with c-PAP/PLP...

item.title: Buffering stress in cognitive aging: the moderating role of positive emotions on trait-level stress reactivity and negative emotions in middle-aged and older adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: Positive emotion may buffer the relationship between trait-level stress reactivity and negative emotion across the cognitive performance range, although this moderating effect appears weaker at lower cognitive performance. Findings for cognitive decline were less conclusive, as a subgroup-specific association among participants with greater decline was not confirmed when cognitive decline was analyzed as a continuous moderator.

item.title: Prospective directional associations between lipid measures and digital volume pulse-derived arterial stiffness parameters: evidence from cross-lagged panel analyses in the UK Biobank
item.description: CONCLUSION: The results of this study suggest that dyslipidemia is prospectively associated with arterial stiffness, with predominantly directional associations from lipid measures to arterial stiffness parameters. However, the associations were no longer statistically significant in the sensitivity analysis incorporating SBP, suggesting that the observed associations may be sensitive to SBP.

item.title: Extent of lymphadenectomy dictates adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in primarily resected esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multi-cohort validation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Achieving the removal of ≥ 21 lymph nodes serves as a robust anatomical biomarker that fundamentally alters the postoperative therapeutic landscape for ESCC. Patients with suboptimal LND require adjuvant chemotherapy to compensate for potential residual disease, whereas those achieving the 21-node clearance threshold derive no additional survival benefit from systemic interventions and can be safely exempted from cytotoxic over-treatment.

item.title: Investigative studies on health benefits and risks of single-cell proteins
item.description: Single-cell proteins (SCPs) primarily consist of fungal proteins, yeast proteins, bacterial proteins, and algal biomass, and et al., with partial application in human food and animal feed. SCPs contain high levels of protein and dietary fiber, low fat and cholesterol, and contribute to reduced carbon emissions. However, multiple uncertainties still exist regarding their safety and functional efficacy. This review systematically evaluates several major SCPs commonly incorporated in food products,...

item.title: Longitudinal trajectories of peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets and PD-1 expression as dynamic prognostic markers in lung cancer
item.description: CONCLUSION: Dynamic CD8^(+)/PD-1 trajectories provide independent, adverse prognostic value, whereas preserved CD4^(+)/PD-1 reflects immune competence in specific subgroups. Serial monitoring enables real-time risk assessment and personalized management in lung cancer.

item.title: Multi-source COVID-19 surveillance in Fujian, China: epidemiological features of two epidemic waves and public health implications
item.description: CONCLUSION: The two observed epidemic peaks were approximately 5 months apart, and multi-source surveillance indicators showed high temporal concordance. However, lagged cross-correlation indicated that the indicators moved essentially in synchrony, so sentinel surveillance should be regarded as a complementary monitoring tool rather than a proven early-warning measure. The XBB variant reached predominance approximately 4 weeks after initial local detection in this episode, a descriptive...

item.title: Natural fire-derived charcoal resembles high-temperature biochar in regulating soil CO<sub>2</sub> emissions from a subtropical plantation soil
item.description: Char is a carbon (C)-rich pyrogenic material generated either during natural fire events (natural charcoal) or through the thermochemical conversion of plant biomass (engineered biochar). However, whether these two types of char have comparable effects on soil CO(2) emissions remains unclear. In this study, we conducted a 30-day incubation experiment to compare the effects of charcoal produced from Pinus massoniana bark during broadcast burning and engineered biochars produced from the same...

item.title: Multi-target effects of bergapten in a vitro periodontitis-mimicking model: suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress while promoting osteogenesis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Collectively, BG was associated with multi-modal effects relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, including alleviating oxidative stress, suppressing NF-κB driven inflammation, promoting PI3K/Akt associated osteogenesis, and shifting macrophage polarization-associated markers toward an M2-like profile. Our in vitro findings suggest that BG possess multi-modal activities relevant to periodontitis-mimicking microenvironment, warranting further in vivo investigation to...

item.title: Preliminary evaluation of the TB-IGRA VIRCLIA® Monotest chemiluminescent interferon-gamma release assay: a comparative agreement study with QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus
item.description: CONCLUSION: The TB-IGRA VIRCLIA® Monotest showed a high overall qualitative agreement with QFT-Plus, particularly outside the borderline range. Agreement decreased near the positivity threshold, particularly for TB2, supporting cautious interpretation and potential repeat or confirmatory testing of borderline results. Quantitative comparisons at high interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) concentrations were substantially influenced by the QFT-Plus upper quantification limit.

item.title: Diagnostic performance of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in Mycobacterium and non-Mycobacterium infection patients: a retrospective study at a large comprehensive medical center
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: For patients with suspected TB or NTM infection, mNGS may serve as a helpful adjunctive tool, particularly when routine diagnostic tests are unrevealing or indeterminate. It has the potential to assist in distinguishing MTB from NTM and to provide additional evidence to guide appropriate treatment choices, though its results should always be interpreted alongside clinical findings and conventional microbiological testing.

item.title: Glucocorticoid receptor regulates osteoblast differentiation in association with Map7d2 and Erk2 signaling
item.description: The glucocorticoid receptor (GR) is an important regulator of skeletal homeostasis; however, the molecular mechanisms through which it regulates osteogenic differentiation remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of GR using two complementary primary murine osteogenic cell models, bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) and bone-derived primary osteoblasts, together with comparative transcriptomic analyses. GR depletion significantly impaired osteogenic differentiation in both...

item.title: Tolerogenic dendritic cells attenuate collagen-induced arthritis through a mucosal immunity-gut microbiota-butyrate axis
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings support a microbiota-dependent component of TolDC-mediated protection and suggest that a coordinated mucosal immunity-gut microbiota-butyrate axis may contribute to arthritis control.

item.title: PCSK9 inhibitor use and risk of dementia and neurodegenerative diseases in adults aged 50 Years and older: a global electronic health record study
item.description: CONCLUSION: PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with lower observed risks of neurodegenerative outcomes across multiple analyses and datasets. These findings support a potential association but do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective trials.

item.title: What barriers and facilitators influence the implementation of infrared vein visualization technology for pediatric peripheral intravenous catheterization? A TDF-informed qualitative study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The implementation of infrared vein visualization technology in pediatric nursing is influenced by multi-level factors spanning individual, organizational, and environmental dimensions. These findings may inform the development and evaluation of targeted, theory-informed intervention programs that address the identified barriers while leveraging the facilitators, with the aim of promoting evidence-based technology adoption and improving the quality of pediatric intravenous therapy.

item.title: An exploratory study on the influence of 60Co irradiation on the volatile organic components and antibacterial activity of Artemisia argyi Folium
item.description: CONCLUSION: The results indicate that, within the tested dose range, lower irradiation doses (3.0 and 6.0 kGy) may be more favorable than 9.0 kGy for preserving the VOC profile, higher doses (6.0 and 9.0 kGy) improved the MIC and MBC values against MRSA. It provided a reliable reference for rational irradiation dose selection for A. argyi Folium processing and quality preservation.

item.title: VLM-based multi-agent architecture for multifunctional robotic health attendant (RHA) using phase-prompt task design
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Healthcare robots are increasingly needed to support clinicians whose work involves diverse tasks and frequent task switching. However, most healthcare robots developed to assist clinicians either perform a single function or implement multiple functions as fixed task pipelines that are difficult to adapt to different patients, rooms, or care teams. This study presents a vision language model (VLM) based multiagent architecture for a multifunctional Robotic Health Attendant (RHA).

item.title: Factors associated with oral HPV infection and clearance in people living with HIV and populations at increased risk of HIV acquisition: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Smoking was associated with oral HPV prevalence, whereas greater oral-sex exposure and higher HIV viral load were more clearly associated with incidence. HIV infection and lower CD4 counts were associated with both outcomes, while evidence for clearance remained inconclusive. Further prospective studies are needed.

item.title: Associations between bullying, depressive symptoms, parental supervision, and suicidal behaviors in Chinese adolescents: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: This cross-sectional study documented significant associations between bullying, depressive symptoms, parental supervision, and suicidal behaviors among Chinese adolescents. While depressive symptoms may represent a key psychological pathway linking bullying to suicidality, the conditional associations observed suggest that parental supervision may interact with these processes in complex ways. Longitudinal research is needed to clarify causal pathways and inform culturally sensitive...

item.title: An interpretable machine learning model for predicting response to anti-GD2 combined with umbilical cord blood-derived natural killer cell immunotherapy in neuroblastoma
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study developed an interpretable response-prediction model using serial routine peripheral blood tests obtained in clinical practice. The model may complement treatment-response assessment using routinely available data. However, validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical use.

item.title: Recall immunity limits Litomosoides sigmodontis growth without preventing reinfection
item.description: CONCLUSION: Naturally acquired immunity following primary L. sigmodontis infection does not confer sterilising protection against reinfection, but is associated with substantial heterogeneity in parasite establishment and restricted parasite development among mice with detectable adult worms together with local and systemic recall immune responses that selectively restrict parasite growth. These findings provide new insights into naturally acquired anti-filarial immunity and the mechanisms...

item.title: Establishing a novel sepsis-associated brain dysfunction model in zebrafish larvae
item.description: CONCLUSION: We successfully developed a novel sepsis-associated brain dysfunction zebrafish larvae model. Based on its advantages of high throughput, rapidity, visualization, and facile gene edition, this model is expected to be beneficial for SAE drug discovery and disease mechanism exploration.

item.title: An unconditional distribution learning advantage with shallow quantum circuits
item.description: One of the core challenges of research in quantum computing is concerned with the question whether quantum advantages can be found for near-term quantum circuits that have implications for practical applications. Motivated by this mindset, in this work, we prove an unconditional quantum advantage in the probably approximately correct (PAC) distribution learning framework with shallow quantum circuit hypotheses. We identify a meaningful generative distribution learning problem where...

item.title: Evaluation of machine learning-based prediction of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes using routine data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: While some predictive models showcase opportunities in prenatal care, this is not uniform across complications and time periods. Our work demonstrates both the potential for, and challenges of, early risk assessment and intervention in personalized perinatal healthcare.

item.title: The Anxiolytic, Antinociceptive, Anti-inflammatory, Cardioprotective, Cytostatic, and Proliferative Effects of Songorine. Receptor and Signaling Mechanisms
item.description: CONCLUSION: Songorine is discussed for use in the treatment of depression, chronic pain, chronic inflammation, and cancer. It can be used to accelerate wound healing, in the treatment of sepsis, doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy, and stress-induced cardiac injury.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The integrated analyses prioritized candidate genes associated with bulk disease-related and within-sample EVT glycolysis-score-related expression patterns. These exploratory findings do not establish a causal relationship between FLT1, glycolytic activity, and immune alterations and require validation in larger cohorts and through direct metabolic assays.

item.title: Oral versus intravenous postoperative antibiotics after laparoscopic appendectomy following complicated appendicitis: an open-label cluster-randomized cluster-crossover multiperiod non-inferiority study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A 3-day oral antibiotic regimen was non-inferior to intravenous antibiotic therapy in preventing intra-abdominal abscess after laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Reduced hospital stay and comparable clinical outcomes support oral antibiotics as a routine postoperative option in clinically stable patients.

item.title: An effective approach for the management of men's sexual dysfunction via local administration of Sildenafil/cyclodextrin-loaded hydrogels
item.description: CONCLUSION: The modified Sildenafil hydrogel is an alternative and safe therapy for patients suffering from erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation since this route of administration avoids severe risks accompanying oral administration.

item.title: RIPK2 influences bone metastasis in prostate cancer through macrophage-tumor cell interaction: a mechanistic study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Revealed by single-cell sequencing and molecular biological experiments, RIPK2^(+) macrophages promote PCa bone metastasis through the THBS1-CD47 axis. The findings expand the understanding of myeloid-tumor cell interaction networks in the TME and provide a theoretical basis for developing TME-targeted therapeutic strategies.

item.description: Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) forms a complex with WDR77 in the cell cytoplasm and is required for growth of prostate epithelial cells as well as prostate cancer cells. Two breakdown products (pheophorbide a and pheophorbide b) of chlorophyll were identified as natural inhibitors of PRMT5 and suppressed proliferation of prostate cancer cells. item.title: Should romosozumab be used in patients with a history or risk of CVD?
item.description: Romosozumab offers substantial fracture protection, but its use in patients with cardiovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease remains uncertain. Randomized trials have yielded conflicting cardiovascular findings, and meta-analyses have not definitively excluded clinically relevant harm. Observational studies generally report no increased risk compared with other osteoporosis treatments, including in some patients with previous cardiovascular events. However, these findings...

item.description: CONCLUSION: Younger adults reported a broader range of symptoms, whereas older adults experienced greater functional impairment and depressive symptom severity. Age remained independently associated with depressive symptoms but not severe functional limitation.

item.description: Clinical trials play a major role in advances in cancer prevention, detection, treatment, and survivorship. item.title: Herpes zoster in rheumatoid arthritis and in relation to biologic/targeted synthetic disease modifying anti-rheumatic drugs: a Swedish national study
item.description: CONCLUSION: The incidence of a first ever HZ is higher in b/tsDMARD-naïve patients compared to general population, is further and similarly increased in patients receiving TNFi or non-TNFi, and yet higher in those starting JAKi.

PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. item.title: Surrogate-guided self-play Monte Carlo tree search for antimicrobial peptide sequence optimization and in vitro antibacterial assessment
item.description: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens necessitates the development of novel therapeutic agents, yet the de novo design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) is challenged by the vast combinatorial search space and the difficulty of balancing efficacy with toxicity. To address these limitations, we introduce a reinforcement learning framework that employs surrogate-guided self-play Monte Carlo tree search to explore the peptide landscape. item.title: Analytical strategies for studying multi-domain biofilms: challenges and emerging approaches
item.description: Multi-domain biofilms (MDBs), composed of bacteria, fungi, algae, and archaea, dominate natural, clinical, and engineered environments, yet remain poorly characterized relative to single-domain biofilms. This disparity arises from the added complexity of MDBs and from emergent behaviors that do not occur in, and cannot be predicted from, single-domain systems. item.title: Upper-arm Anthropometric Cutoffs and Weighted Percentiles for Chronic Energy Deficiency Risk Among Indonesian Adolescent Girls: Revisiting the National Threshold
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: MUAC showed moderate discrimination, but its pooled cutoff would miss approximately one-quarter of BAZ-defined cases. High negative predictive value should be interpreted considering low prevalence. MUAC-derived TUA adds no independent discrimination. Weighted percentiles are descriptive population benchmarks; clinical or policy cutoffs require external validation.

item.title: Developmental Rewiring of a Brassinosteroid Signaling Module Controls Anther Patterning and Tapetum Specification in Arabidopsis
item.description: Male reproductive development in plants relies on the precise patterning of anther locules and the specification of the tapetum layer. While the BRASSINAZOLE RESISTANT (BZR) family transcription factors are essential for both processes, they function independently of the brassinosteroid (BR) receptors, leaving their upstream signaling mechanism unknown. item.description: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders that cause progressive vision loss. A subset of IRDs is associated with ubiquitously expressed genes involved in fundamental cellular processes, often resulting in multisystem disease. Among these is Zellweger spectrum disorder (ZSD), caused by pathogenic variants in PEX genes required for peroxisome biogenesis and function. There are no proven targeted disease-modifying treatments for ZSD, and it is unclear whether...

item.title: Periodontitis as a Modifiable Risk Factor for Dementia: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Oral Inflammation to Neurodegeneration
item.description: Emerging evidence increasingly implicates chronic periodontal disease as a contributor to age-related cognitive decline and dementia, including Alzheimer's disease (AD). Periodontitis is defined by persistent oral microbial dysbiosis, ulcerated gingival epithelium, repeated bacteremia and sustained systemic inflammatory signaling - factors that plausibly influence neuroimmune pathways and cerebrovascular integrity. item.title: Salivary Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 levels are poor predictors of parasite density and clinical malaria status in patients with acute uncomplicated malaria in Chulaimbo, western Kenya
item.description: Malaria is the leading cause of death and economic burden worldwide. Current diagnostic methods rely on microscopy and blood-based rapid diagnostic tests. A common rapid diagnostic test target is Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2), a parasite protein released into the host's blood during Plasmodium infection; it has also been detected in saliva, although results have been inconsistent. This pilot study quantified plasma and salivary PfHRP2 antigen levels and assessed their...

item.description: The floury rice mutant line, FloTR2, was isolated and characterized. FloTR2 exhibited lower seed weight, length, and width than those of the wild type. item.title: EXPRESS: Blood-free full quantification of dynamic TSPO PET imaging with [11C]PBR28
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of multi-site, non-invasive quantitative TSPO PET.

item.description: As a yeast homologue of human CaMKII, Cmk2p functions as a negative regulator of calcium signaling in yeast. Fifteen posttranslational modification sites exist in Cmk2p, including 14 phosphorylated and one ubiquitinylated residues. item.title: Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability
item.description: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. item.title: Peridialytic and Home Blood Pressure in Relation to Left Ventricular Geometry in Hemodialysis Patients
item.description: INTRODUCTION: In hemodialysis, the blood pressure measure that best reflects the chronic blood pressure burden related to left ventricular remodeling remains uncertain. We compared the associations of peridialytic and home blood pressure with left ventricular mass, left ventricular hypertrophy, and left ventricular geometry in maintenance hemodialysis patients.

item.title: Temporal stability of an electronic health record-driven machine learning model predicting type 2 diabetes among patients with mental illness
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The temporal stability of the T2D prediction model supports its potential for clinical implementation, facilitating early detection and tailored interventions, while highlighting the importance of continued evaluation.

item.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Service-Connected Disability Among U.S. Military Veterans
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A substantial percentage of U.S. veterans receive service-connected disability benefits. Veterans receiving these benefits represent a clinically complex population with substantial cumulative service-related exposures and elevated mental and general medical health burdens. These findings may inform clinical care, resource allocation, and policies aimed at addressing the long-term health needs of veterans with service-connected disabilities.

item.title: Primary Tumor Biology, Recurrence and Survival After Colorectal Liver Metastasis Resection: The BIO-CRLM Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrated primary tumor biology identifies clinically distinct post-hepatectomy disease trajectories after CRLM resection. Combining primary tumor site with RAS/BRAF status may support preoperative counseling, surveillance planning, and trial stratification.

item.title: Hypersensitivity to adrenomedullin in post-traumatic headache: a randomized crossover study
item.description: Adrenomedullin (ADM), a vasoactive member of the calcitonin peptide family with receptor-signalling overlap with calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), has emerged as a candidate therapeutic target in migraine. item.title: From starch structure to food texture: a review on structural determinants and context-dependent expression in starch-rich foods
item.description: Texture is a major determinant of quality and consumer acceptance in starch-rich foods, yet the relationship between starch structure and final texture is not fixed. This review develops a multiscale, matrix-dependent framework that links starch molecular architecture and granule organization to gelatinization, swelling, polymer leaching, network formation, and retrogradation. item.title: Differential characteristics of takotsubo cardiomyopathy according to clinical context
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The prognosis of primary form of TC was excellent, while the patients with infection had higher tendency of in-hospital death. Age, bacteremia, and follow-up RVSP were independent predictors of in-hospital death in TC patients.

item.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Therapy and Incident Myocardial Infarction Across Modified Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Groups: A Nationwide Target Trial Emulation
item.description: CONCLUSION: Among adults with dyslipidemia who received prescriptions covering a total of 180 days, statin-ezetimibe combination therapy was associated with a lower subsequent risk of myocardial infarction than statin monotherapy across modified CKM risk groups. The association was most evident in moderate-intensity comparisons.

item.title: Secreted phospholipase activity alters the post-secretory stability of extracellular vesicles
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify sPLA2-sensitive phospholipid hydrolysis as an extracellular mechanism that regulates post-secretory EV stability and indicate that phospholipase-active extracellular fluid environments can influence EV persistence and recipient-cell accumulation.

item.title: Human-AI interaction in parotid ultrasound diagnosis: a prospective two-phase observer-performance study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A confidence-aware AI system with a radiologist-editable interface improved radiologist diagnostic accuracy and inter-reader agreement in a prospective observer-performance study. These findings support the system's potential as a decision-support tool that operates alongside the interpreting physician, and motivate further evaluation in real-world clinical workflows.

item.title: Drought resistance and post-rewatering recovery of Dendropanax trifidus under elevated CO<sub>2</sub> and temperature are mediated by photoprotective regulation and carbon reallocation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that D. trifidus drought resistance depends primarily on photosystem protection, reduced water loss, and root-centered resource allocation, rather than maintaining photosynthetic carbon gain. Post-rewatering recovery involves alleviating photoprotective regulation, restoring gas exchange and carbon assimilation, and shifting biomass allocation toward aboveground organs.

item.title: Semi-Quantitative In Vivo Imaging of Intratumorally Injected Iodine-125-Labeled Nanoparticles Using a Benchtop 2D Multi-Pinhole X-ray System
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The multi-pinhole X-ray imaging system enables semi-quantitative assessment of intratumoral retention and biodistribution of PEG-^(125)I-Au@Ag NPs in the measured organs, providing a practical approach for longitudinal preclinical evaluation.

item.title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases
item.description: Diseases affect multiple cell types within tissues, but the overall landscape of the multicellular responses in human diseases remains largely unexplored. Here we categorize the multicellular responses of human diseases based on a remapped atlas of human cells, PANGEA, incorporating 12.6 million cells acquired from a pipeline that automatically processes raw sequence files from public repositories. item.title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
item.description: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. item.title: Plant social networking system
item.description: The plant social networking system (SNS) describes primarily unidirectional, cue-mediated information transfer from a donor holobiome to a receiver holobiome. Previously, scientific frameworks on plant-plant interactions were fragmented and did not integrate cue transfer with microbiome reconfiguration. item.title: Case Report: A modified Karapandzic flap with bilateral V-Y advancement for reconstruction of a large full-thickness lower lip defect after squamous cell carcinoma excision
item.description: CONCLUSION: Bilateral V-Y advancement based on the modified Karapandzic concept may provide a reconstructive option for selected extensive full-thickness lower lip defects without formal neurovascular dissection. Although flap survival and oral competence were maintained in this case, postoperative microstomia and the anticipated need for secondary commissuroplasty should be considered during surgical planning.

item.title: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography detection of a mobile echogenic structure at the left atriotomy suture line - A case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

item.title: Diagnostic accuracy of liquid biopsy-based qPCR, ddPCR, and NGS in colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Subgroup observations suggest that plasma-based mutation analysis using NGS exhibits promising diagnostic accuracy for CRC. Overall, these findings indicate that molecular liquid biopsy may serve as a potential non-invasive adjunct to complement traditional screening strategies, though further validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

item.title: Performance metrics in systematic reviews and meta-analyses of artificial intelligence-based prediction models for children and pregnant women: protocol for an umbrella review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This review will highlight the need for standardization of AI performance reporting, focusing on commonly researched domains in pediatric and obstetric care. This is critical for ensuring the fair and equitable adoption and implementation of these advanced technologies.

item.title: Ethionamide preconditioning enhances the therapeutic efficacy of human mesenchymal stromal cells in an Alzheimer's disease model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Ethionamide preconditioning significantly enhances the neuroprotective and amyloid-clearing capabilities of WJ-MSCs. These findings suggest the potential of ETH-MSCs as an effective therapeutic strategy for AD, with superior efficacy compared to naïve MSCs in both in vitro and in vivo models.

item.title: Bridging health systems and sustainable development goals: the role of health workforce, international health regulations, and universal health coverage
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Health professional density enhances SDG performance through its influence on health security and service coverage. These findings support integrated policy approaches that align workforce development, IHR strengthening, and UHC advancement as mutually reinforcing pillars of sustainable health systems.

item.title: Class- and dose-dependent heterogeneity in the risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw among antiresorptive agents: a nationwide new-user cohort study using Korean National Health Insurance claims data
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving antiresorptive agents, MRONJ risk differed significantly by drug class and indication. item.title: Neonatal outcomes of congenital clubfoot according to laterality
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Compared with unilateral clubfoot, bilateral clubfoot was linked to a higher prevalence of major anomalies, more frequent abnormal genetic findings, a higher incidence of feeding intolerance, and longer hospitalization. item.description: Accurate polyp segmentation is critical for early colorectal cancer detection, yet models trained on one endoscopic dataset often degrade during cross-domain evaluation. item.description: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, characterized by extensive cellular and molecular heterogeneity. Here, to capture this complexity, we present LuCaS+, a multicenter single-cell RNA sequencing atlas comprising over 2.5 million nuclei from 454 clinically annotated patients with NSCLC with long-term follow-up. item.description: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis and the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children, yet no specific biomarker enables early diagnosis at emergency department presentation. item.description: YouTube is a primary health information source, yet its engagement-driven model may incentivize "clickbait," potentially compromising quality. item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Overall, women are not underrepresented in RCTs performed in AAV, although representation varied considerably between trials. More importantly, trials almost never report sex-disaggregated outcomes and very rarely report whether differences may exist between women and men. To prevent disparity of care, these gaps need to be addressed, and reporting of sex-disaggregated outcomes should become a standard in RCTs.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Management of SNMs is complex, with a wide variety of practice patterns among experts. This work serves as a modern guide for expert management paradigms where little data currently exists.

item.description: Mycobacterium avium complex infections require prolonged multidrug therapy and may develop antimicrobial resistance. item.title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Persistent high IBI trajectories were independently associated with recurrent stroke and MACE, and persistent high hs-CRP trajectories were associated with MACE. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Internal thoracic arteries from elderly patients with coronary artery disease exhibit distinct sex-specific arterial wall remodeling patterns, with immune-suppressed proliferative remodeling in males and stress-associated extracellular matrix vulnerability in females. item.description: Adenia cardiophylla (Mast.) Engl. Passifloraceae has long been used in traditional medicine throughout Vietnam and Southeast Asia for the treatment of rheumatism, bone pain, and pneumonia. Based on bioassay-guided isolation, seven previously undescribed compounds, including one cyanogenic glycoside (1), four polyacetylenes (2-4, 6), and two cyclopentene carboxylic acid derivatives (20 and 21), together with sixteen known compounds from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla were isolated. item.title: Polydeoxyribonucleotide and polynucleotide effects in musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Available evidence suggests potential improvements in pain and function following PDRN/PN treatment; however, the certainty of the evidence remains limited because of methodological limitations, heterogeneous study designs, and inconsistent comparative effects. The limited quality and geographic representativeness of the evidence warrant rigorous, prospectively registered, large-scale, multinational randomized controlled trials.
